description: ODC: the Comment of the canvas of a UI flow (IMobileFlow) — the note that the author pastes beside the screens to explain the design. It is a full IMobileFlowNode, not a widget: it lives in the FLOW, never inside a screen. Four things that only the real model teaches and that this job proves: (1) the type has to come QUALIFIED, OutSystems.Model.UI.Mobile.IComment, because the bare name IComment ties with OutSystems.Model.UI.Web.IComment at Rank 2 of FindCreateCore (Verbs.cs:877-880); (2) layout is not called (AGENTS.md:247 limits it to action/preparation/process) because the position already comes from .AtDefaultPosition(), in IMobileFlow.CreateNode<T> (NRFlows.cs:1257); (3) the Comment has NO name — the name of the create is discarded, the get returns name=null and the DisplayName of the object becomes the text itself; (4) the property of the interface is Text (IComment.cs:32), and the Comment that appears in the get is the SAME slot seen through the single concrete class (ServiceStudio.Model.Nodes+Comment, the one that also serves the BPT node), not a second property. What the platform fills in by itself: CreatedBy, LastModifiedBy and LastModifiedDate with the identity of whoever is editing, and a default position. What does NOT follow along: that position is the SAME for all comments of the flow (the second one is born on top of the first), so whoever wants two legible notes has to separate them with move x/y — and the connector that links the note to a screen (Connectors stays 0 in both gets).

expectedMessages.why: Setting IsReminder=true makes the platform emit a 'Reminder' message in TrueChange with the text of the comment itself: that is what the box is for, and it is exactly what this job proves. The comment with IsReminder=false emits nothing. It is not a defect of the job: it is the meaning of the property.
